text:
Corn earworm / Heliothis (Helicoverpa armigera), rated as a high-importance pest.

Description: the caterpillar (larval) stage is variably coloured (green, brown, or pink with striping) and is found across a wide range of host crops, not just corn. Larvae typically feed at the silk and developing kernels at the tip of the ear.

Damage: larvae feeding on silks and developing kernels reduces grain quality and yield directly, and the feeding wounds they create on the ear tip also provide an entry point for secondary fungal infections such as ear rot. Younger larvae may also feed on leaves before moving to the ear.
